prompt: You are configuring a home network for a customer. The customer has requested the ability to access a Windows PC remotely, and needs all chat and optional functions to work in their game console.
INSTRUCTIONS
Use the drop-down menus to complete the network configuration for the customer. Each option may only be used once, and not all options will be used.
Then, click the + sign to place each device in its appropriate location.
Wireless AP LAN
summary: Use the drop-downs to set the wireless AP LAN IP and encryption, the router port-forward rule, and the firewall LAN IP, then place the PC and game console in the correct network locations.

pairs.item: Device placement on the Wireless AP

steps: 1. Only private, routable address ranges can serve as a LAN gateway, so the wireless AP takes 192.168.10.1 while the screened subnet firewall gets the separate 10.100.0.1 network to keep the two segments distinct.
2. Remote Desktop for the Windows PC uses TCP port 3389, so the router's port-forward rule must be Allow TCP Any 3389 and the PC is placed behind the router where that rule points.
3. Home wireless clients need a pre-shared key rather than an enterprise RADIUS setup or a VPN/TLS protocol, so WPA2 PSK is the correct encryption type.
4. The game console requires open chat and optional (NAT-friendly) services, so it is attached to the wireless AP segment protected by WPA2 PSK rather than isolated in the screened subnet.
5. The firewall is positioned in front of the screened subnet with its 10.100.0.1 interface facing that subnet so externally reachable hosts stay separated from the trusted LAN.

The customer has two requirements: remote access to a Windows PC and full chat/optional features on a game console. Remote Desktop listens on TCP 3389, so the router's inbound port-forward rule is set to Allow TCP Any 3389 and the PC sits behind that router so forwarded traffic reaches it. The wireless AP serves the trusted LAN, so it is given the private gateway address 192.168.10.1 and secured with WPA2 PSK, the appropriate pre-shared-key encryption for a home network; the game console is joined to that AP so its chat and optional services are not blocked by the tighter restrictions of an isolated segment. The firewall belongs in front of the screened subnet with the distinct 10.100.0.1 address facing that subnet, which keeps any externally exposed hosts on their own network separate from the home LAN.

prompt: A technician needs to provide remote support for a legacy Linux-based operating system from their Windows laptop. The solution needs to allow the technician to see what the user is doing and provide the ability to interact with the user's session.
Which of the following remote access technologies would support the use case?
explanation: VNC (Virtual Network Computing) is the correct choice because it provides remote desktop access with GUI interaction capabilities, allowing the technician to see the user's screen and control the session. VNC works cross-platform, making it ideal for connecting

from Windows to Linux systems. While SSH provides secure remote access, it is command-line only and does not provide the visual interaction required. VPN only encrypts network traffic but does not provide remote desktop capabilities. RDP is Windows-specific and would not natively support legacy Linux systems.

why.A: VPN only provides encrypted network connectivity, not remote desktop or session interaction.
why.C: SSH provides command-line access only, not the GUI visual interaction and control needed.
why.D: RDP is designed for Windows systems and does not natively support Linux operating systems.

prompt: A technician is attempting to join a workstation to a domain but is receiving an error message stating the domain cannot be found. However, the technician is able to ping the server and access the internet. Given the following information:
Which of the following should the technician do to fix the issue?
explanation: When a workstation cannot find a domain despite having internet connectivity and being able to ping servers, the issue is typically related to DNS resolution. Domain joining requires the workstation to resolve the domain name to locate the domain controller through DNS queries. If DNS is not configured correctly (pointing to the wrong DNS server or not pointing to a DNS server that can resolve the domain), the domain lookup will fail. Since the technician can ping and access the internet, the network connectivity is working, but DNS resolution for the domain is the problem. Changing the DNS settings to point to the correct DNS server (typically the domain controller or a DNS server authoritative for that domain) will resolve the issue.

why.B: A static IP address assignment does not resolve domain name resolution issues; the problem is DNS configuration, not IP address assignment method.

prompt: A network technician notices that most of the company's network switches are now end-of-life and need to be upgraded.
Which of the following should the technician do first?
explanation: Proposing the change is the first step in proper change management procedures. Before any approval, scheduling, or implementation can occur, the technician must formally propose the change to document the need, scope, and justification for upgrading the end-of-life switches. This establishes the change request that will then go through approval and scheduling workflows.

why.A: Implementation cannot occur first; changes must be proposed, approved, and scheduled before implementation.
why.B: Approval comes after the change has been proposed and documented.
why.D: Scheduling occurs after the change is proposed and approved, not before.

prompt: MFA for a custom web application on a user's smartphone is no longer working. The last time the user remembered it working was before taking a vacation to another country.
Which of the following should the technician do first?

options.text: Verify the date and time settings.

answerText: Verify the date and time settings.
explanation: Verifying the date and time settings is the correct first step because MFA systems, particularly time-based authentication methods like TOTP, are highly sensitive to device time synchronization. When the user traveled to another country, their device may have retained the original timezone or incorrect time, causing MFA tokens to become invalid. This is a simple check that often resolves authentication issues before attempting more complex troubleshooting steps.

why.B: Mobile OS patches may help but are not the first troubleshooting step for a time-sensitive MFA issue.
why.C: Reinstalling the application is premature without checking basic time synchronization first.
why.D: Escalation to the developer should occur only after basic troubleshooting steps have been exhausted.

prompt: Which of the following is found in an MSDS sheet for a battery backup?
explanation: An MSDS (Material Safety Data Sheet) sheet contains emergency procedures, which is critical information for hazardous materials like batteries. MSDS sheets are designed to provide safety information including hazard identification, first-aid measures, and emergency procedures. This is essential for battery backups due to their potentially hazardous chemical contents. Installation instructions, configuration steps, and voltage specifications are technical product information typically found in user manuals or technical documentation, not MSDS sheets.

why.A: Installation instructions are found in user manuals or product documentation, not MSDS sheets.
why.C: Configuration steps are technical specifications found in product guides, not MSDS sheets.
why.D: Voltage specifications are electrical specifications found in technical datasheets, not MSDS sheets.

prompt: The screen of a previously working computer repeatedly displays an OS Not Found error message when the computer is started. Only a USB drive, a keyboard, and a mouse are plugged into the computer.
Which of the following should a technician do first?

options.text: Run data recovery tools on the disk.
Partition the disk using the GPT format.

explanation: Checking boot options is the first step when encountering an 'OS Not Found' error. The computer may be configured to boot from the wrong device or in the wrong order. With only a USB drive, keyboard, and mouse connected, the system might be attempting to boot from a device that no longer contains a valid OS. Checking and correcting the boot order in BIOS/UEFI is the quickest troubleshooting step before attempting data recovery, disk partitioning, or firmware changes.

why.A: Data recovery tools are a last resort and should not be attempted first when basic boot configuration may be the issue.
why.B: Repartitioning the disk would be destructive and should only be considered after confirming boot configuration issues.
why.D: Switching UEFI to BIOS is not a first troubleshooting step and may not be necessary if boot options are correctly configured.

prompt: A security administrator teaches all of an organization's staff members to use BitLocker To Go.
Which of the following best describes the reason for this training?

options.text: To ensure that all removable media is password protected in case of loss or theft
To enable Secure Boot and a BIOS-level password to prevent configuration changes
To enforce VPN connectivity to be encrypted by hardware modules
To configure all laptops to use the TPM as an encryption factor for hard drives

answerText: To ensure that all removable media is password
explanation: protected in case of loss or theft

BitLocker To Go is specifically designed to encrypt removable media such as USB drives and external hard drives. Training staff on this tool ensures that if removable media is lost or stolen, the data remains protected through encryption. This addresses the critical security need of protecting sensitive data that leaves the organization. BitLocker To Go creates password-protected encrypted volumes on portable devices to prevent unauthorized access in case of loss or theft.

why.B: Secure Boot and BIOS-level passwords are system-level security features, not the purpose of BitLocker To Go training.
why.C: BitLocker To Go does not enforce VPN connectivity or involve hardware encryption modules for VPN.
why.D: BitLocker To Go can work with TPM but is not specifically designed to configure laptop hard drives; it is primarily for removable media.

prompt: Which of the following is used to detect and record access to restricted areas?
explanation: Video surveillance is the primary technology used to detect and record access to restricted areas. Security cameras provide continuous monitoring and recording of who enters and exits restricted zones, creating an audit trail of access events. This technology serves both as a deterrent and as evidence in security incidents. While badge readers control access, they do not detect or record visual access. Bollards and fences are physical barriers that prevent access but do not provide detection or recording capabilities.

why.A: Bollards are physical barriers that prevent vehicle access but do not detect or record access attempts.
why.C: Badge readers control access permissions but do not inherently detect or record visual access to areas.
why.D: Fences are physical perimeter barriers that prevent access but do not detect or record unauthorized access attempts.

prompt: An administrator received an email stating that the OS they are currently supporting will no longer be issued security updates and patches.
Which of the following is most likely the reason the administrator received this message?

options.text: Support from the computer’s manufacturer is expiring.
The OS will be considered end of life.
The built-in security software is being removed from the next OS version.
A new version of the OS will be released soon.

answerText: The OS will be considered end of life.
explanation: When an operating system no longer receives security updates and patches, it has reached end of life status. End of life means the manufacturer is ceasing support and no longer issuing updates, security patches, or technical support for that OS version. This is an official lifecycle stage that indicates the OS version is aging out of support. While support expiration is related, the specific message about no longer issuing security updates directly indicates the OS has transitioned to end of life status.

why.A: While related, 'support expiring' is less precise than 'end of life' which specifically refers to cessation of all updates and patches.
why.C: Removal of built-in security software is a feature change, not the reason for ceasing security updates to the entire OS.
why.D: A new OS version release is independent of the current OS reaching end of life, though they may occur around the same time.

prompt: Which of the following is the best way to distribute custom images to 800 devices that include four device vendor classes with two types of user groups?

options.text: Use xcopy to clone the hard drives from one to another.
Use robocopy to move the files to each device.
Use a local image deployment tool for each device.
Use a network-based remote installation tool.

answerText: Use a network-based remote installation tool.
explanation: For distributing custom images to 800 devices across multiple vendor classes and user groups, a network-based remote installation tool (such as Windows Deployment Services, SCCM, or similar solutions) is the most efficient and scalable approach. It allows centralized management, supports multiple device types, and can be configured with different profiles for different user groups without manual intervention on each device.

why.A: xcopy is a file-copying utility designed for small-scale transfers, not bulk OS image deployment to hundreds of devices.
why.B: robocopy is a file synchronization tool, not an imaging solution, and would not efficiently deploy complete OS images across 800 devices.
why.C: Using a local tool on each device would be extremely time-consuming and impractical for 800 devices and would lack centralized control.

prompt: Which of the following types of social engineering attacks sends an unsolicited text message to a user's mobile device?
explanation: Smishing is the specific term for SMS phishing—sending malicious or deceptive text messages to mobile devices to trick users into clicking links or providing information. It combines 'SMS' and 'phishing' and is the direct answer to unsolicited text message attacks.

why.A: Impersonation is a general social engineering technique but does not specifically describe text message attacks.
why.B: Vishing is voice phishing conducted through phone calls, not text messages.
why.C: Spear phishing typically refers to targeted email attacks, not SMS-based attacks.

prompt: A user reports some single sign-on errors to a help desk technician. Currently, the user is able to sign in to the company's application portal but cannot access a specific SaaS-based tool.
Which of the following would the technician most likely suggest as a next step?

options.text: Reenroll the user's mobile device to be used as an MFA token.
Use a private browsing window to avoid local session conflicts.
Bypass single sign-on by directly authenticating to the application.
Reset the device being used to factory defaults.

answerText: Use a private browsing window to avoid local session
explanation: conflicts.

When a user can access the main portal via SSO but cannot access a specific SaaS application, the issue is often caused by local session state, cached cookies, or browser-specific conflicts. Using a private browsing window eliminates cached credentials and local session data, allowing the browser to create a clean SSO flow to the SaaS application without interference from previous sessions.

why.A: Reenrolling an MFA device would only be necessary if MFA itself was failing, not if SSO to one specific application is broken.
why.C: Bypassing SSO entirely defeats the purpose of troubleshooting the SSO issue and is not a diagnostic step.
why.D: Factory reset is an extreme measure inappropriate as a first troubleshooting step for an application-specific SSO problem.

prompt: A technician verifies that a malware incident occurred on some computers in a small office.
Which of the following should the technician do next?

options.text: Update the anti-malware and scan the computers.

explanation: The immediate first step in malware incident response is to quarantine infected systems to prevent the malware from spreading to other computers on the network. This containment step must happen before any other remediation activities to limit the scope of the incident.

why.B: User education is important for prevention but comes after containment, not as the next immediate step.
why.C: Disabling System Restore is a remediation step done after quarantine, to prevent malware restoration from recovery points.
why.D: Updating anti-malware and scanning should occur after quarantine, not before, to prevent spread during the scan process.

prompt: Which of the following is a Linux command that is used for administrative purposes?
explanation: The 'su' command (substitute user) is the standard Linux administrative command used to switch to another user account, most commonly to root/superuser, enabling administrative tasks. It is the Linux equivalent of elevation of privilege.

why.A: runas is a Windows command, not Linux.
why.B: cmcl is not a recognized standard Linux administrative command.
why.C: net user is a Windows command for user account management, not a Linux command.

prompt: A user recently installed an application that accesses a database from a local server.
When launching the application, it does not populate any information.
Which of the following command-line tools is the best to troubleshoot the issue?
explanation: netstat is the best tool to troubleshoot database connectivity issues. It displays active network connections, listening ports, and connection states, allowing the technician to verify whether the application is successfully establishing a connection to the local
database server on the expected port.

why.A: ipconfig displays IP configuration but does not show active connections or whether the application can reach the database server.
why.B: nslookup is for DNS resolution; it would not help if the database server is accessed by IP or if DNS is not the issue.
why.D: curl is a data transfer tool primarily for HTTP/HTTPS requests; it would not diagnose database connection issues on local servers.

prompt: A small office reported a phishing attack that resulted in a malware infection. A technician is investigating the incident and has verified the following:
All endpoints are updated and have the newest EDR signatures.
Logs confirm that the malware was quarantined by EDR on one system.
The potentially infected machine was reimaged.
Which of the following actions should the technician take next?

options.text: Install network security tools to prevent downloading infected files from the internet.
Discuss the cause of the issue and educate the end user about security hygiene.
Flash the firmware of the router to ensure the integrity of network traffic.
Suggest alternate preventative controls that would include more advanced security software.

answerText: Discuss the cause of the issue and educate the end
explanation: user about security hygiene.

After verifying that the technical controls (EDR, patching) are working properly and the infected machine has been remediated, the next critical step is to educate the user about the root cause (phishing in this case) and proper security hygiene. This addresses the human vulnerability that allowed the attack to succeed in the first place and prevents recurrence.

why.A: Network security tools are not the next step when EDR already caught the malware; the issue was user susceptibility to phishing, not file download capability.
why.C: Firmware flashing is unnecessary and does not address the phishing vulnerability that caused the incident.
why.D: More advanced security software is not needed when current controls (EDR with latest signatures) already successfully quarantined the threat.

prompt: Which of the following describes a vulnerability that has been exploited before a patch or remediation is available?
explanation: A zero-day vulnerability is, by definition, a vulnerability that has been discovered and exploited by attackers before the vendor is aware of it or has released a patch. The term 'zero-day' refers to the fact that vendors have had zero days to develop and release a fix.

why.A: Spoofing is an attack technique (impersonation), not a vulnerability classification.
why.B: Brute-force is an attack method, not a type of vulnerability.
why.C: DoS (Denial of Service) is an attack, not a vulnerability type or a descriptor of patch availability.

prompt: You have been contacted through the help desk chat application. A user is setting up a replacement SOHO router. Assist the user with setting up the router.
INSTRUCTIONS
Select the most appropriate statement for each response.
Click the send button after each response to continue the chat.
summary: Select the most appropriate response for each step of a SOHO router setup chat interaction.

pairs.match: I am happy to assist you today.
Is this the first router in your office?
The first thing you need to do is change the default password.
Create a new password with an uppercase, a lowercase, and a special character.

steps: 1. Open the conversation by offering a helpful and professional greeting that sets a positive tone.
2. Gather context about the router deployment by asking whether this is the first router at the location.
3. After confirming it is a replacement router and the user is logged in, advise changing the default credentials immediately.
4. Provide specific password requirements that ensure security: uppercase, lowercase, and special character complexity.
5. When the router prompts for reboot, confirm the action with a brief affirmative response to complete setup.
These responses follow a logical sequence for secure router configuration. The first response establishes a professional and welcoming tone. The second response gathers

information to tailor guidance appropriately. The third response prioritizes security by recommending credential change as the first step after login, which is essential for any networked device. The fourth response gives concrete, actionable password requirements that meet industry standards for complexity. The fifth response confirms the final action, allowing the router to restart with new security settings in place. Together, these responses guide the user through proper SOHO router setup with emphasis on security best practices.

prompt: A help desk technician is setting up speech recognition on a Windows system.
Which of the following settings should the technician use?
explanation: Speech recognition is an accessibility feature in Windows and is configured through the Ease of Access settings. This is where users can enable and configure speech recognition, voice commands, and other accessibility options designed to assist users with disabilities or accessibility needs.

why.A: Time and Language settings control regional preferences, language packs, and input methods, not speech recognition.
why.B: Personalization settings manage themes, colors, lock screen, and start menu appearance, not accessibility features.
why.C: System settings cover general device information, storage, and power options, not speech recognition configuration.

prompt: A user receives a new personal computer but is unable to run an application. An error displays saying that .NET Framework 3.5 is required and not found.
Which of the following actions is the best way to resolve this issue?

options.text: Resolve the dependency through the "Turn Windows features on or off" menu.
Download the dependency via a third-party repository.
Ignore the dependency and install the latest version 4 instead.
Forward the trouble ticket to the SOC team because the issue poses a great security risk.

answerText: Resolve the dependency through the "Turn Windows
explanation: features on or off" menu.

The Windows Features dialog (accessible through 'Turn Windows features on or off') allows users to install optional Windows components, including .NET Framework 3.5. This is the proper, supported method for resolving .NET Framework dependencies on Windows systems.

why.B: Third-party repositories are unreliable sources for critical system dependencies and bypass proper Windows package management.
why.C: Ignoring a specific version requirement and installing a newer version may cause compatibility issues if the application requires .NET 3.5 specifically.
why.D: A missing .NET Framework is not a security risk and does not require escalation to a Security Operations Center team.

prompt: An employee is using a photo editing program. Certain features are disabled and require a log-in, which the employee does not have.
Which of the following is a way to resolve this issue?
explanation: License assignment through proper account credentials or administrative assignment enables access to features that are locked behind licensing requirements. When an application requires a login to unlock certain features, this typically indicates license-dependent functionality that can be resolved by assigning the appropriate license to the user's account.

why.B: A VPN connection is for network access and would not unlock application features that require licensing or authentication.
why.C: Application repair addresses corrupted files or installation issues, not license-gated features.
why.D: Program reinstallation alone will not resolve licensing issues without proper license assignment or credentials.

prompt: A technician is deploying mobile devices and needs to prevent access to sensitive data if the devices are lost.
Which of the following is the best way to prevent unauthorized access if the user is unaware that the phone is lost?
explanation: Remote wipe is the best proactive protection against unauthorized access to sensitive data when a device is lost and the user is unaware of the loss. It allows IT to remotely erase all data on the device before a threat actor can access it, ensuring data confidentiality even if the device cannot be physically recovered.

why.A: Encryption protects data at rest but does not prevent access if the device is already compromised or the password is weak; it also requires the user to be aware of loss.
why.C: Geofencing alerts on location anomalies but does not prevent data access and requires the user to take action after being notified.
why.D: Facial recognition only prevents unauthorized unlock attempts but does not prevent data access if biometric authentication is bypassed or spoofed.

prompt: Which of the following is the quickest way to move from Windows 10 to Windows 11 without losing data?
explanation: An in-place upgrade is the quickest method to move from Windows 10 to Windows 11 while preserving user data, applications, and settings. It upgrades the operating system
while maintaining the existing installation, whereas other methods would require more time or result in data loss.

why.A: gpupdate is a Group Policy update command and is not a method for upgrading operating systems.
why.B: Image deployment requires creating, managing, and deploying system images, which is more time-consuming than an in-place upgrade.
why.C: A clean install erases all data and applications, requiring reinstallation of software and reconfiguration of settings, thus violating the requirement to not lose data.

prompt: Technicians are failing to document user contact information, device asset tags, and a clear description of each issue in the ticketing system.
Which of the following should a help desk management team implement for technicians to use on every call?
explanation: Standard operating procedures (SOPs) establish consistent, documented guidelines and checklists that technicians must follow on every call. SOPs specifically address documentation requirements such as contact information, asset tags, and issue descriptions, ensuring consistency across all help desk interactions.

why.A: Service-level agreements define response and resolution time targets but do not establish documentation procedures or requirements.
why.B: Call categories are classification systems for organizing ticket types but do not mandate specific documentation fields or processes.
why.D: Knowledge base articles provide solutions and reference information but do not establish documentation standards or requirements for technicians.

prompt: An application's performance is degrading over time. The application is slowing, but it never gives an error and does not crash.
Which of the following tools should a technician use to start troubleshooting?
explanation: Resource Monitor provides real-time visibility into CPU, memory, disk, and network usage by individual processes and applications. When an application is slowing without errors or crashes, Resource Monitor is the best tool to identify which system resources are being consumed excessively, guiding further investigation.

why.A: Reliability history shows system crashes and warnings but not real-time resource consumption or gradual performance degradation without errors.
why.B: Computer Management is a general administration tool useful for services and processes but does not provide detailed real-time resource monitoring.
why.D: Disk defragmentation is a maintenance operation and not a diagnostic tool; it also assumes the issue is disk-related without investigation.

prompt: Which of the following filesystem types does the Linux OS use?
explanation: ext4 (fourth extended filesystem) is the standard and most commonly used filesystem for Linux operating systems. It is the default filesystem for most modern Linux distributions and is designed specifically for Linux, offering reliability, performance, and scalability.

why.A: exFAT is a filesystem primarily used for USB drives and memory cards, designed by Microsoft for cross-platform compatibility, not Linux.
why.B: APFS (Apple File System) is the filesystem used by macOS and iOS, not Linux.
why.D: NTFS (New Technology File System) is the filesystem used by Windows operating systems, not Linux.

prompt: Which of the following methods would make data unrecoverable but allow the drive to be repurposed?
explanation: A low-level format writes over all sectors of the drive at the hardware level, making data unrecoverable while preserving the drive's functionality for repurposing. This method overwrites the entire disk surface, eliminating all data recovery possibilities while keeping the drive usable.

why.A: Deleting partitions only removes the partition table and logical structures; data remains physically on the drive and can be recovered with forensic tools.
why.B: EFS (Encrypting File System) encrypts data but does not make it unrecoverable—the drive cannot be easily repurposed without decryption keys.
why.D: Degaussing uses a magnetic field to erase data but typically destroys the drive's functionality, making it unsuitable for repurposing.

prompt: After a recent mobile OS upgrade to a smartphone, a user attempts to access their corporate email, but the application does not open. A technician restarts the smartphone, but the issue persists.
Which of the following is the most likely way to resolve the issue?

options.text: Registering the smartphone with an MDM solution

explanation: After a mobile OS upgrade, the most likely issue is that the email application is incompatible with the new OS version or requires an update. Updating the failed software addresses version mismatches and compatibility issues that emerge after OS upgrades.

why.B: MDM registration manages device policies and security but does not resolve application compatibility or functionality issues after an upgrade.
why.C: Installing a third-party client is unnecessary when the original application may simply need updating to work with the new OS.
why.D: Clearing the cache partition addresses storage and temporary data issues, not compatibility problems caused by OS upgrades.

prompt: Users are reporting that an unsecured network is broadcasting with the same name as the normal wireless network. They are able to access the internet but cannot connect to the file share servers.
Which of the following best describes this issue?
explanation: A rogue wireless access point broadcasting the same SSID as the legitimate network can intercept connections while appearing legitimate. Users can access the internet through it but cannot reach internal file servers, which indicates an unauthorized access point that lacks proper network configuration or intentionally restricts access to internal resources.

why.A: An unreachable DNS server would prevent internet access entirely, not selective access where internet works but file shares don't.
why.B: VLAN misconfiguration would not cause an entirely separate unsecured network to broadcast with the same name.
why.C: Incorrect IP addresses would not result in internet connectivity while blocking file server access in this manner.

prompt: A computer technician is implementing a solution to support a new internet browsing policy for a customer's business. The policy prohibits users from accessing unauthorized websites based on categorization.
Which of the following should the technician configure on the SOHO router?
explanation: Content filtering on a SOHO router allows administrators to block access to websites based on categorical rules. This directly implements the policy requirement to prohibit users from accessing unauthorized websites by categorization.

why.A: Secure management access protects the router's administrative interface but does not control user internet access.
why.B: Group Policy Editor is a Windows domain tool for managing networked computers, not for configuring router-level web restrictions.
why.D: A firewall controls network traffic and ports but is not the primary tool for blocking websites by category or content type.

prompt: Recently, the number of users sharing smartphone passcodes has increased. The management team wants a technician to deploy a more secure screen lock method.
Which of the following technologies should the technician use?
explanation: Facial recognition provides biometric authentication that cannot be shared between users, directly addressing the problem of users sharing passcodes. It is inherent to the individual and cannot be easily compromised through code sharing.

why.A: Pattern lock can still be shared visually or through observation, similar to passcodes.
why.C: Device encryption protects data but does not address the screen lock sharing issue.
why.D: Multifactor authentication adds security layers but does not prevent passcode sharing; additional factors could still be compromised.

prompt: An end user's laptop is having network drive connectivity issues in the office. The end user submits a help desk ticket, and a support technician is able to establish a remote connection and fix the issue. The following day, however, the network drive is disconnected again.
Which of the following should the technician do next?

options.text: Connect remotely to the user’s computer to see whether the network drive is still connected.
Send documentation about how to fix the issue in case it reoccurs.
Escalate the ticket to the next level.
Keep the ticket open until next day, then close the ticket.

answerText: Escalate the ticket to the next level.
explanation: When an issue recurs immediately after resolution, it indicates a persistent underlying problem that requires deeper investigation beyond the initial fix. Escalation to a higher support level ensures the root cause is identified rather than applying temporary solutions repeatedly.

why.A: Simply reconnecting remotely to verify current status does not address the recurring nature of the problem.
why.B: Documentation for end-user self-service is inappropriate when a technical issue demonstrates a pattern requiring professional diagnosis.
why.D: Keeping the ticket open without action and closing it arbitrarily does not resolve the recurring issue.

prompt: Which of the following provides information to employees, such as permitted activities when using the organization's resources?
explanation: An Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) defines permitted and prohibited activities when using organizational resources. It communicates expectations to employees regarding appropriate use of company equipment and systems.

why.B: MNDA (Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement) governs confidentiality between parties, not permitted activities for resource usage.
why.C: DRM (Digital Rights Management) controls access to copyrighted content, not organizational resource usage policies.
why.D: EULA (End User License Agreement) governs software licensing terms, not organizational resource usage policies.

prompt: A technician needs to install an operating system on a large number of workstations.
Which of the following is the fastest method?
explanation: Image deployment captures a pre-configured operating system and applications as a single image that can be rapidly deployed to multiple workstations simultaneously. This is significantly faster than installing the OS individually on each machine.

why.A: Physical media requires individual manual installation on each workstation, which is time-consuming.
why.B: A mountable ISO still requires manual installation steps on each workstation rather than automated bulk deployment.
why.C: Manual installation on each workstation is the slowest possible method for a large number of systems.

prompt: A user is working from home and is unable to access work files on a company laptop.
Which of the following should a technician configure to fix the network access issue?
explanation: A Virtual Private Network (VPN) is the standard solution for securely accessing company resources from a remote location like a home office. VPNs encrypt the connection and authenticate the user before granting access to internal company files and systems. This is the industry-standard approach for remote work security.

why.A: A WAN connects multiple office locations together, not individual remote workers to company resources.
why.B: A wireless network is a local connectivity method and doesn't address accessing company files securely from home.
why.C: Proxy settings manage web traffic filtering but don't provide secure authenticated access to internal company file systems.

prompt: A technician is troubleshooting an issue in which a service runs momentarily and stops at certain points in the process. The technician needs to determine the root cause of this issue.
Which of the following tools should the technician use?
explanation: Event Viewer is the primary Windows tool for diagnosing service failures and interruptions. It logs detailed information about services stopping unexpectedly, including error codes and timestamps that help identify the root cause of why a service stops at certain points in its execution.

why.B: Task Manager shows running processes and performance but doesn't provide the detailed diagnostic logs needed to understand why a service fails at specific points.
why.C: Internet Options configures browser settings and has no relevance to troubleshooting service failures.
why.D: Process Explorer shows process details and relationships but lacks the historical event logging necessary to determine why a service stops intermittently.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of an application publisher including undisclosed additional software in an installation package?
explanation: A Potentially Unwanted Program (PUP) is software bundled into installation packages without clear disclosure or user consent. Publishers often include PUPs like toolbars, adware, or tracking software alongside legitimate applications, which is the definition of undisclosed additional software bundled in an installation package.

why.A: A virus is malicious code that replicates and damages systems, not specifically software bundled within installation packages by publishers.
why.B: Ransomware encrypts files for extortion; it's not characterized by being bundled as additional software in legitimate installation packages.
why.D: A Trojan is malicious software disguised as legitimate, but the term doesn't specifically describe undisclosed bundled software in installation packages like PUPs do.

prompt: A technician needs to map a shared drive from a command-line interface.
Which of the following commands should the technician use?
explanation: The 'net use' command is the standard Windows command-line tool for mapping network drives and shared resources. It allows technicians to establish persistent or temporary connections to shared folders on remote servers from a command-line interface.

why.A: Pathping tests network connectivity and routing but does not map network drives.
why.B: Nslookup performs DNS name resolution lookups and does not map network drives.
why.D: Tracert traces the route packets take to a destination but does not map network drives.

prompt: A help desk team was alerted that a company-owned cell phone has an unrecognized password-cracking application.
Which of the following should the help desk team do to prevent further unauthorized installations from occurring?
explanation: Mobile Device Management (MDM) solutions are specifically designed to manage, monitor, and secure company-owned mobile devices. MDM enforces security policies, restricts unauthorized app installations, manages permissions, and can remotely wipe devices—making it the appropriate solution to prevent future unauthorized installations on company cell phones.

why.A: Group Policy is a Windows domain management tool and cannot manage iOS or Android mobile devices effectively.
why.B: PAM (Privileged Access Management) controls administrative access to systems, not app installations on mobile devices.
why.C: While anti-malware software helps detect threats, MDM is the comprehensive solution that prevents unauthorized installations through policy enforcement.

prompt: Which of the following is used in addition to a password to implement MFA?

options.text: Sending a code to the user's phone
Verifying the user's date of birth
Prompting the user to solve a simple math problem
Requiring the user to enter a PIN

answerText: Sending a code to the user's phone
explanation: Multi-Factor Authentication requires two or more distinct verification methods. Sending a code to the user's phone (such as via SMS or authenticator app) is a common second factor used in addition to a password, providing authentication based on something the user has (their phone).

why.B: Verifying date of birth is static information that users have and is not truly a separate authentication factor from a password.
why.C: Solving a math problem is still something the user knows and doesn't constitute a separate factor from a password.
why.D: A PIN is also something the user knows, which is the same category as a password and doesn't add a separate authentication factor.

prompt: A technician is preparing to replace the batteries in rack-mounted UPS system. After ensuring the power is turned off and the batteries are fully discharged, the technician needs to remove the battery modules from the bottom of the rack.
Which of the following steps should the technician take?

options.text: Ensure the fire suppression system is ready to be activated.
Use appropriate lifting techniques and guidelines.
Place the removed batteries in an antistatic bag.
Wear a face mask to filter out any harmful fumes.

answerText: Use appropriate lifting techniques and guidelines.
explanation: When replacing heavy batteries from a rack-mounted UPS system, the technician must prioritize safety by using appropriate lifting techniques and guidelines to prevent back injury or dropping batteries. This is a critical safety requirement when handling heavy components at the bottom of a rack.

why.A: Fire suppression systems are not relevant to battery replacement procedures when power is off and batteries are discharged.
why.C: While antistatic bags protect electronics from static discharge, batteries are not sensitive to static electricity and this is not the priority safety concern.
why.D: A face mask is not necessary when batteries are fully discharged; harmful fumes are not a concern in this scenario.

prompt: A technician is setting up a surveillance system for a customer. The customer wants access to the system's web interface on the LAN via the system’s IP address.
Which of the following should the technician use to prevent external log-in attempts from the internet?
explanation: Port mapping (or port forwarding) controls which ports are accessible from external networks. By not mapping the surveillance system's web interface port to the internet-facing router, external login attempts are prevented while the system remains accessible locally on the LAN via the internal IP address.

why.B: Subnetting divides networks into segments but doesn't inherently prevent external access unless combined with firewall rules; it doesn't block internet login attempts.
why.C: A static IP ensures consistent addressing but doesn't prevent external login attempts or restrict access from the internet.
why.D: Content filtering controls the type of traffic allowed but is not the primary mechanism for preventing external access to a specific internal service.

prompt: A technician needs to configure laptops so that only administrators can enable virtualization technology if needed.
Which of the following should the technician configure?
explanation: Virtualization technology is a BIOS/UEFI setting that controls CPU-level virtualization features. A BIOS password restricts access to BIOS settings, ensuring only administrators with the password can enable or disable virtualization. This provides hardware-level
access control that prevents unauthorized users from modifying critical system features.

why.B: Guest accounts have minimal privileges but don't control BIOS settings access.
why.C: Screen locks protect against physical access but don't restrict BIOS configuration.
why.D: AutoRun settings control automatic execution of media, not virtualization technology.

prompt: Which of the following file types would a desktop support technician most likely use to automate tasks for a Windows user log-in?
explanation: Batch files (.bat) are the standard Windows native scripting format for automating tasks during user logon. They execute in the Windows command prompt and are commonly used in logon scripts, startup sequences, and scheduled tasks. While other languages can automate Windows tasks, .bat is the most direct and commonly deployed solution for Windows logon automation.

why.B: .sh files are shell scripts for Unix/Linux systems, not Windows.
why.C: .py files require Python interpreter installation and are not Windows-native.
why.D: .js files are JavaScript, typically for web browsers or Node.js, not standard Windows logon automation.

prompt: A technician uses AI to draft a proposal about the benefits of new software.
When reading the draft, the technician notices that the draft contains factually incorrect information.
Which of the following best describes this scenario?
explanation: Hallucinations occur when AI systems generate plausible-sounding but factually incorrect information. This is a well-documented limitation of large language models where the AI confidently produces false data that appears coherent. The scenario describes exactly this phenomenon—factually incorrect information in an otherwise credible-sounding draft.

why.A: Data privacy concerns protecting personal information, not factual inaccuracy in generated content.
why.C: Appropriate use refers to ethical guidelines for using AI, not inherent technical limitations.
why.D: Plagiarism involves copying existing work; hallucinated content is original but false.

prompt: Which of the following describes an attack in which an attacker sets up a rogue AP that tricks users into connecting to the rogue AP instead of the legitimate network?
explanation: An evil twin is a rogue access point that mimics a legitimate wireless network's SSID and characteristics to trick users into connecting. Attackers use this technique to intercept traffic or perform man-in-the-middle attacks. The name 'evil twin' directly describes this impersonation attack method.

why.A: Stalkerware is surveillance software installed on a device, not a network attack.
why.C: Tailgating involves physical access exploitation, not wireless network impersonation.
why.D: Shoulder surfing is observing someone's screen or keyboard, not a wireless attack.

prompt: A user is experiencing issues with outdated images while browsing websites.
Which of the following settings should a technician use to correct this issue?
explanation: Internet Options is the Windows control panel for managing browser settings, including cache and temporary files. When users see outdated images on websites, it's typically because cached versions are not being refreshed. Clearing the browser cache through Internet Options resolves this issue by forcing fresh downloads of current images.

why.A: Administrative Tools manage system services and performance, not browser cache.
why.B: Windows Defender Firewall controls network traffic, not cached browser images.
why.D: Ease of Access provides accessibility features, not browser cache management.

prompt: Every time a user loads a specific spreadsheet, their computer is temporarily unresponsive. The user also notices that the title bar indicates the applications are not responding.
Which of the following would a technician most likely inspect?

options.text: Bandwidth status as reported in the Task Manager
File size and related memory utilization

answerText: File size and related memory utilization
explanation: When a specific spreadsheet causes temporary unresponsiveness and the title bar shows 'not responding,' it indicates the application is consuming excessive system resources. File size and memory utilization inspection through Task Manager reveals whether the spreadsheet is consuming excessive RAM or causing memory-related performance issues. This diagnostic approach identifies resource-based performance problems.

why.A: Anti-malware logs check for malicious activity, not resource consumption issues.
why.B: Workstation repair options are too generic and don't address specific spreadsheet performance.
why.C: Bandwidth status in Task Manager monitors network usage, not the local memory/file size causing unresponsiveness.

prompt: A user frequently misplaces their Windows laptop and is concerned about it being stolen. The user would like additional security controls on their laptop.
Which of the following is a built-in technology that a technician can use to enable full drive encryption?
explanation: BitLocker is Microsoft's built-in full disk encryption technology available on Windows Pro, Enterprise, and Education editions. It encrypts entire drives to protect data if a device is lost or stolen, making it the standard solution for comprehensive drive encryption on Windows laptops.

why.A: Active Directory manages user authentication and group policies, not drive encryption.
why.B: NTFS is a file system; while it supports encryption, it's not full disk encryption like BitLocker.
why.C: Encrypting File System (EFS) provides file-level encryption, not full drive encryption.

prompt: Which of the following is used to apply corporate restrictions on an Apple device?
explanation: A management profile (also called Mobile Device Management or MDM profile) is the mechanism for applying corporate restrictions and policies to Apple devices. It allows IT administrators to enforce security policies, configure settings, restrict app installations, and manage device compliance without requiring physical device access.

why.A: App Store is for downloading applications, not enforcing corporate restrictions.
why.B: VPN configuration is one specific network setting but doesn't provide comprehensive corporate restrictions.
why.C: Apple ID is for personal account authentication and services, not corporate policy enforcement.

prompt: A user's new smartphone is not staying charged throughout the day. The smartphone charges fully every night.
Which of the following should a technician review first to troubleshoot the issue?
explanation: Background applications consume battery power and should be the first diagnostic step when a device charges fully but does not hold charge throughout the day. Since the device charges properly, the charger and power delivery are functioning correctly. Storage usage and software support status are less likely to cause rapid battery drain compared to runaway background processes.

why.A: Storage usage affects performance and available space but not battery drain rate.
why.B: End of software support would be a longer-term concern, not an immediate battery drain issue.
why.C: The device charges fully each night, indicating the charger wattage is adequate.

prompt: A customer is unable to open some files on their system. Each time the customer attempts to open a file, the customer receives a message that the file is encrypted.
Which of the following best describes this issue?
explanation: Ransomware specifically encrypts user files and displays messages demanding payment
or action to decrypt them. This is the defining characteristic of ransomware attacks. The scenario directly describes encrypted files with system messages, which is the hallmark ransomware behavior.

why.A: Keyloggers record keystroke input; they do not encrypt files or display messages about encryption.
why.C: Phishing is a social engineering attack via email or messages; it does not encrypt files on the system.
why.D: Cryptominers use system resources to mine cryptocurrency but do not encrypt user files or generate encryption-related messages.

prompt: An organization is experiencing an increased number of issues. A technician notices applications that are not installed by default. Users are reporting an increased number of system prompts for software licensing.
Which of the following would the security team most likely do to remediate the root cause?

options.text: Deploy an internal PKI to filter encrypted web traffic.
Remove users from the local admin group.
Implement stronger controls to block suspicious websites.
Enable stricter UAC settings on Windows.

answerText: Remove users from the local admin group.
explanation: Unauthorized applications being installed and software licensing prompts indicate users with administrative privileges are installing unauthorized or potentially malicious software. Removing users from the local admin group prevents them from installing software without proper authorization, addressing the root cause of unwanted application installations.

why.A: Internal PKI filtering encrypted traffic would not prevent unauthorized software installation on local systems.
why.C: Blocking suspicious websites may help with phishing but does not prevent local admin users from installing applications.
why.D: While stricter UAC settings may provide some protection, removing admin rights is the more direct and effective solution.

prompt: A support specialist needs to decide whether to install a 32-bit or 64-bit OS architecture on a new computer.
Which of the following specifications will help the specialist determine which OS architecture to use?
explanation: 16GB of RAM is the key specification for determining OS architecture. 64-bit operating systems can address and utilize significantly more RAM than 32-bit systems (which are limited to 4GB). With 16GB of RAM, a 64-bit architecture is necessary. The CPU, storage, and network specifications do not directly determine which architecture to use.

why.B: Both 32-bit and 64-bit OS can run on an Intel i7 CPU; the CPU alone does not determine architecture choice.
why.C: Storage capacity does not determine whether to use 32-bit or 64-bit architecture.
why.D: Network speed does not influence the choice between 32-bit and 64-bit operating systems.

prompt: Which of the following prevents forced entry into a building?
explanation: A bollard is a physical barrier (typically a post or pillar) that prevents vehicles and people from forcibly entering a building by blocking entry points. It provides active physical obstruction against forced entry. The other options provide detection or access control but not actual physical prevention of forced entry.

why.A: PIV cards provide logical access control for authorized personnel but do not prevent forced physical entry.
why.B: Motion-activated lighting is a deterrent and detection tool but does not prevent actual forced entry.
why.C: Video surveillance records entry but does not prevent someone from forcibly entering the building.

prompt: A technician is assigned to offboard a user.
Which of the following are common tasks on an offboarding checklist? (Choose two.)

options.text: Quarantine the hard drive in the user's laptop.
Deactivate the user's key fobs for door access.
Purge all PII associated with the user.
Turn off the network ports underneath the user’s desk.
Add the MAC address of the user's computer to a blocklist.

answerText: Deactivate the user's key fobs for door access.; Suspend the user's email account.
explanation: Deactivating key fobs (B) removes physical access to the building and secure areas, a critical security measure. Suspending the email account (D) prevents unauthorized use of company communications and ensures the user cannot send messages or access corporate information. These are standard offboarding tasks to protect company security and data.

why.A: Quarantining the hard drive is not a common offboarding task; data should be wiped or preserved according to retention policies, not quarantined.
why.C: Purging all PII associated with the user may violate data retention and compliance requirements.
why.E: Turning off network ports is not a standard offboarding task; deactivating accounts provides logical access control.
why.F: Adding the MAC address to a blocklist is unnecessary if network access is properly disabled through account deactivation.

prompt: A company would like to deploy baseline images to new computers as they are started up on the network.
Which of the following boot processes should the company use for this task?
explanation: PXE (Preboot Execution Environment) is the boot protocol that allows computers to boot from a network server and download baseline images. This enables automated deployment of standardized images to new computers as they start up on the network without requiring physical media.

why.A: ISO is a file format for disk images, not a boot process for network deployment.
why.B: Secure Boot is a UEFI security feature that validates firmware signatures; it is not used for deploying baseline images.
why.C: USB boot requires physical media to be present at each computer; it is not suitable for automated network-wide deployment.

prompt: A user has been adding data to the same spreadsheet for several years. After adding a significant amount of data, they are now unable to open the file.
Which of the following should a technician do to resolve the issue?

options.text: Revert the spreadsheet to the last restore point.

explanation: Large spreadsheets with years of accumulated data consume significant memory. When the file becomes too large for available RAM, the spreadsheet application cannot load or process it. Increasing RAM allows the application to allocate sufficient memory to open and work with the large file.

why.A: Reverting to a restore point would lose all the data the user has added, which is not an appropriate solution.
why.C: Defragmentation affects file storage fragmentation but not memory availability for opening large applications.
why.D: Network connection speed has no impact on a local application's ability to open a file stored on the user's computer.

prompt: A technician installs VPN client software that has a software bug from the vendor. After the vendor releases an update to the software, the technician attempts to reinstall the software but keeps getting an error message that the network adapter for the VPN already exists.
Which of the following should the technician do next to mitigate this issue?

options.text: Run the latest OS security updates.
Map the network adapter to the new software.

explanation: When VPN software reinstallation fails due to an existing network adapter error, the issue is typically caused by remnants of the previous installation, including hidden network adapters that weren't properly removed. Deleting these hidden adapters clears the conflict, allowing the new software to install successfully without the adapter already exists error.

why.A: OS security updates do not address residual VPN adapter configurations from previous installations.
why.B: Mapping the network adapter to new software is not a standard troubleshooting step and doesn't resolve adapter conflicts.
why.C: Network adapter firmware updates are not relevant to resolving software installation conflicts caused by leftover adapter configurations.

prompt: Which of the following is the best reason for a network engineering team to provide a help desk technician with IP addressing information to use on workstations being deployed in a secure network segment?

options.text: Only specific DNS servers are allowed outbound access.
The network allow list is set to a specific address.
DHCP services are not enabled for this subnet.
NAC servers only allow for security updates to be installed.

answerText: DHCP services are not enabled for this subnet.
explanation: If DHCP services are not enabled for a subnet, workstations cannot automatically receive IP addresses and must be manually configured with static IP addressing information provided by the network engineering team. This is the primary reason to provide specific IP addressing details for secure network segment deployments.

why.A: DNS server restrictions relate to outbound access policies, not the core reason for providing IP addressing information to help desk technicians.
why.B: Network allow lists typically work with configured addresses regardless of how those addresses were obtained, not the primary reason for manual IP assignment.
why.D: NAC server security update policies are unrelated to the need for manual IP addressing configuration.

prompt: A technician is using a credential manager to safeguard a large number of credentials.
Which of the following is important for using this application?
explanation: A secure master password is the critical foundational security requirement for a credential manager. It serves as the single authentication factor that protects access to all stored credentials, making it essential for safeguarding the entire vault of sensitive information.

why.A: Restricted login times are a nice-to-have security control but are not as fundamental as the master password for protecting stored credentials.
why.C: While TPM can enhance security, it is not universally required for credential managers to function securely.
why.D: Windows lock screen security is an OS-level control and not specific to the credential manager application itself.

prompt: Which of the following methods involves requesting a user's approval via a push notification to verify the user's identity?
explanation: An authenticator app (such as Microsoft Authenticator or Google Authenticator) is the method that specifically sends push notifications to a user's device requesting approval to verify identity. This is push-based notification authentication, distinct from other MFA methods.

why.A: Call-based verification involves voice interaction, not push notifications.
why.C: Hardware tokens typically generate time-based codes rather than sending push notifications for approval.
why.D: SMS delivers codes or links via text message but does not use push notifications to the user's application.

prompt: A customer wants to be able to work from home but does not want to be responsible for bringing company equipment back and forth.
Which of the following would allow the user to remotely access and use a Windows PC at the main office? (Choose two.)
explanation: RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol) is the native Windows remote desktop solution that allows direct access to a Windows PC. VPN (Virtual Private Network) is often used alongside or instead of RDP to provide secure remote access to office resources. Both options enable a user to remotely control a Windows PC without transporting company equipment, making them the correct combination.

why.A: SPICE is a remote desktop protocol used primarily with Linux/KVM environments, not Windows PCs.
why.B: SSH is a command-line remote access protocol, not a graphical remote desktop solution for Windows workstations.
why.E: RMM (Remote Monitoring and Management) is for IT support and device management, not for the user to work on their own office PC.
why.F: WinRM is a Windows remote management protocol used for administrative tasks, not for interactive remote desktop work.

prompt: A company wants to use a single operating system for its workstation and servers and avoid licensing fees.
Which of the following operating systems would the company most likely select?
explanation: Linux is the operating system that meets all the company's requirements: it can be used for both workstations and servers, and it is free and open-source, eliminating licensing fees. Windows, macOS, and Chrome OS all require licensing fees or are limited to specific device types.

why.B: Windows requires licensing fees for both workstation and server editions.
why.C: macOS is limited to Apple hardware and requires licensing; it is not suitable for server deployments in most enterprise scenarios.
why.D: Chrome OS is designed primarily for lightweight client devices and is not suitable for server deployments.

prompt: A user is attempting to open on a mobile phone a HD video that is hosted on a popular media streaming website. The user is receiving connection timeout errors. The mobile reception icon area is showing two bars next to 3G.
Which of the following is the most likely cause of the issue?

options.text: The user does not have Wi-Fi enabled.
The website's subscription has run out.
The bandwidth is not fast enough.
The mobile device storage is full.

answerText: The bandwidth is not fast enough.
explanation: The user is on 3G with only two signal bars, which indicates weak and slow cellular connectivity. HD video streaming requires substantial bandwidth; 3G networks with poor signal strength cannot provide sufficient bandwidth to stream HD content smoothly, resulting in timeout errors. This is the most direct cause of the streaming failure.

why.A: Wi-Fi not being enabled does not cause the connection timeout; the user is receiving timeouts on cellular 3G, indicating a connection attempt is being made.
why.B: Subscription status issues would typically result in authentication or access denied errors, not connection timeouts.
why.D: Device storage being full would affect local playback or caching, not cause streaming connection timeouts from a remote server.

prompt: A technician notices that the weekly backup is taking too long to complete. The daily backups are incremental.
Which of the following would most likely resolve the issue?
explanation: Synthetic full backups create a complete backup image by combining the previous full backup with all incremental backups, without requiring a full re-scan of source data. This process is faster than a traditional full backup while maintaining the efficiency of incremental daily backups, making it the best solution for reducing lengthy weekly backup windows.

why.A: Changing the backup window only shifts when the backup runs; it does not address the underlying performance issue.
why.B: Performing incremental weekly backups would reduce backup size but increases complexity in recovery and does not address restoration speed.
why.C: Increasing backup storage capacity does not reduce the time required for the backup process to complete.

prompt: A help desk technician needs to remove RAM from retired workstations and upgrade other workstations that have applications that use more memory with this RAM.
Which of the following actions would the technician most likely take?

options.text: Use antistatic bags for storage and transport.
Plug in the power supply to ground each workstation.

answerText: Use antistatic bags for storage and transport.
explanation: When removing and reusing RAM from retired workstations, the technician must protect the memory modules from electrostatic discharge (ESD) damage during storage and transport. Antistatic bags are the industry standard for this purpose, preventing static electricity from damaging the sensitive electronic components on the RAM modules.

why.A: Demagnetization is not a security procedure for RAM and would not protect the memory modules.
why.C: Grounding workstations via power supply is unnecessary for RAM removal and does not protect the memory modules themselves.
why.D: Installing memory in identical pairs is a best practice for some systems but is not the primary action when initially removing and storing RAM.

prompt: A customer’s computer does not have an active connection to the network. A technician goes through a few troubleshooting steps but is unable to resolve the issue. The technician has exhausted their knowledge. The customer expresses frustration at the time taken to resolve this issue.
Which of the following should the technician do?

options.text: Escalate the issue to a senior team member and provide next steps to the customer.
Dismiss the customer and reschedule another troubleshooting session at a later date.
Interrupt the customer and express that troubleshooting support tickets can take time.
Maintain a positive attitude and continue to ask questions regarding the scope of the issue.

answerText: Escalate the issue to a senior team member and
explanation: provide next steps to the customer.

When a technician has exhausted their troubleshooting knowledge and the customer is frustrated, the professional response is to escalate the issue to a senior team member who may have additional expertise, while providing the customer with clear next steps and expectations. This demonstrates competence, respect for the customer's time, and a commitment to resolution.

why.B: Dismissing the customer and rescheduling is disrespectful and leaves the issue unresolved.
why.C: Interrupting the customer and making excuses worsens their frustration rather than addressing it constructively.
why.D: While maintaining a positive attitude is good, continuing to ask questions when knowledge is exhausted wastes time and further frustrates the customer.

prompt: A company executive is currently attending a major music festival with a large number of attendees and is having trouble accessing a work email account. The email application is not downloading emails and also appears to become stuck during connection attempts.
Which of the following is most likely causing the disruption?

options.text: The phone has no storage space available.
Company firewalls are configured to block remote access to email resources.
Too many devices in the same area are trying to connect to the mobile network.
The festival organizer prohibits internet usage during the event and has blocked the internet signal.

answerText: Too many devices in the same area are trying to
explanation: connect to the mobile network.

At a large music festival with thousands of attendees, the mobile network is likely congested with too many devices attempting to connect simultaneously. This causes connection timeouts, failed downloads, and stuck connection attempts—exactly the symptoms described. Network congestion is a common issue in high-density areas.

why.A: While storage space issues can prevent email downloads, they would not cause the application to become stuck during connection attempts.
why.B: Corporate firewalls typically block internal/VPN access from unknown networks, but would not cause the specific stuck connection behavior at a festival venue.
why.D: If the internet signal were completely blocked, the application would fail immediately rather than appear to get stuck during connection attempts.

prompt: A company recently transitioned to a cloud-based productivity suite and wants to secure the environment from external threat actors.
Which of the following is the most effective method?
explanation: Multifactor authentication (MFA) is the most effective method for securing cloud-based environments against external threat actors. MFA requires users to provide multiple forms of verification, making it extremely difficult for attackers to gain unauthorized access even if they obtain passwords, thereby protecting accounts from credential-based attacks.

why.B: Encryption protects data confidentiality but does not prevent unauthorized access to accounts themselves.
why.C: Backups provide data recovery capabilities but do not prevent external threat actors from accessing the system.
why.D: Strong passwords alone are insufficient protection; they can still be compromised through phishing, brute force, or credential breaches.

prompt: As a corporate technician, you are asked to evaluate several suspect email messages on a client's computer. Corporate policy requires the following:
All phishing attempts must be reported.
Future spam emails to users must be prevented.
INSTRUCTIONS
Review each email and perform the following within the email:
Classify the emails -Identify suspicious items, if applicable, in each email
Select the appropriate resolution If at any time you would like to bring back the initial state of the simulation, please click the Reset All button.
summary: For each of the five inbox messages, choose a classification (Phishing, Spam or Legitimate) and the correct resolution action.
steps: 1. Check the sender domain of the "Account Locked" message: ithelpdesk@comptia.co is a look-alike of comptia.org, and the message urges the user to click a link to change a password, so it is phishing and must be reported to Information Security per policy.

2. The "Share Your Feedback" survey is an external but digitally signed marketing message from survey@researchco.net with a working Manage Email Preferences link, so the exhibit treats it as legitimate and no further action is needed.
3. The "Employee Orientation" note comes from the internal hr@comptia.org address with a PDF reference guide and no coercive language, making it legitimate correspondence requiring no action.

4. The "Security Update" message is sent from the misspelled domain comptiaa.org and pushes an unsolicited patch1.exe attachment; the exhibit classifies it as spam and, because it is a malicious mass mailing, it is reported to Information Security.
5. The "Interview" thank-you note from a personal Gmail account contains no links or attachments and matches a real interaction, so it is legitimate with no additional actions.

The exercise tests whether you can separate malicious mail from harmless mail by inspecting sender addresses, attachments and the urgency of the request. Two messages are hostile: the "Account Locked" alert spoofs the help desk using the comptia.co domain and drives the user to a password-reset link, which is classic credential phishing, and the "Security Update" comes from comptiaa.org with an executable attachment, which the official answer labels spam. Corporate policy says phishing attempts must be reported and future spam must be stopped, so both of those go to Information Security rather than being unsubscribed or opened. The remaining three messages — the signed external survey, the internal HR orientation with a PDF, and the personal interview thank-you — show no spoofing, no malicious payload and no coercion, so they are legitimate and require no additional actions.

prompt: A user reports getting a BSOD error on their computer at least twice a day.
Which of the following should the technician use to determine the cause?
explanation: Event Viewer is the Windows system tool that logs detailed information about system errors, including Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) events. It records crash information, error codes, and system events that help technicians identify the underlying cause of recurring BSOD errors.

why.B: Performance Monitor tracks system performance metrics but does not specifically record BSOD crash information.
why.C: System Information displays hardware and software configuration details but does not log error events.
why.D: Device Manager shows installed hardware and drivers but does not log system crash events or BSOD information.

prompt: A technician is setting up a Windows server to allow remote desktop connections for multiple users.
Which of the following should the technician configure on the workstation?
explanation: To enable Remote Desktop connections, the technician must configure the Windows Firewall to allow inbound Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) traffic on port 3389. Without firewall configuration, the firewall will block incoming RDP connection attempts, preventing remote users from accessing the server.

why.B: Computer Management is used for system administration tasks but Remote Desktop is enabled through firewall rules and system settings, not Computer Management.
why.C: User Accounts may need to be configured for permissions, but the primary configuration for Remote Desktop connectivity is firewall-related.
why.D: Ease of Access provides accessibility features but is not involved in configuring Remote Desktop connections.

prompt: A technician thinks that an application a user downloaded from the internet may not be the legitimate one, even though the name is the same. The technician needs to confirm whether the application is legitimate.
Which of the following should the technician do?

options.text: Compare the hash value from the vendor.
Run Task Manager and compare the process ID.
Run the application in safe mode.
Verify the file name is correct.

answerText: Compare the hash value from the vendor.
explanation: Comparing the hash value of a downloaded application against the hash value published by the vendor is the most reliable method to verify software authenticity. Hash values act as digital fingerprints—if the application is legitimate, its hash will match the vendor's published hash exactly. Any modification or counterfeit version will produce a different hash.

why.B: Process IDs in Task Manager are dynamically assigned and vary between systems; they cannot be used to verify application legitimacy.
why.C: Running an application in safe mode does not verify its legitimacy; a malicious application could still run in safe mode.
why.D: Verifying the file name is superficial; malware can use legitimate-sounding names and cannot confirm the actual identity of the application.

prompt: Multiple users are reporting audio issues as well as performance issues after downloading unauthorized software. You have been dispatched to identify and resolve any issues on the network using best practice procedures.
INSTRUCTIONS
